description.narrative:
Halting biodiversity loss is a Sustainable Development Goal (SDG 15), one that is strongly linked to all other SDGs. Keeping ecosystems resilient and safeguarding our planet’s biodiversity is fundamental to poverty eradication, human health and wellbeing. The Lima Action Plan for UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme and its World Network of Biosphere Reserves (2016-2025) contains a comprehensive set of actions aimed at ensuring the effective implementation of the MAB Strategy 2015-2025. The backbone of this strategy are UNESCO designated sites which provide over 1,000 places for its implementation around the globe.
Nigeria with a land size of about 923,768 km² and population of about 213,000,000 currently has four Biosphere reserves and more than 14 National Parks, 8 strict nature reserves, and 38 game reserves. The country has high potential of having more biosphere reserves to safeguard the biodiversity of the country, build resilience to impact of climate change and contribute to wellbeing. The Workplan, “Supporting Nomination of sites in Nigeria to join UNESCO WNBR”, will be implemented within the framework of the 42 C/5, towards supporting nomination of at least 2 additional biosphere reserves.
UNESCO Abuja and Accra offices, worked in close collaboration with the UNESCO HQ Earth Sciences and Geoparks section (SC/EES/EG) to organize a two-day Concertation on UNESCO Global Geoparks (UGGp) in West Africa, in 2023. At the end of the Concertation, the list of action was agreed upon which include that NatCom-UNESCO should facilitate the establishment of Geopark National committee in their respective countries. To this end and to provide a valid platform for Nigeria to start up activities towards having its first UGGp as well as participate in IGCP projects, UNESCO Abuja office will support Nigeria in the Inauguration of international Geoscience and Geopark Nigeria National Committee. UNESCO Global Geopark National Committees is very crucial for designation of sites as UGGp because the committee provide platform for facilitating Geological heritage survey, present application for UGGp, promote Geopark projects, and promote international cooperation between and among geoparks. On the other hand, the International Geoscience Programme (IGCP) National Committees stimulates the participation of their country’s geoscientists in new IGCP projects and enables them to share ongoing international geoscience research of note
The Workplan will contribute to SDGs- 15.1, 15.2, 15.9, and 17.9, and the following goals of AU Agenda 2063 - Aspiration 7, Goal 19, Priority Area 36 – Partnership - AU 2063 Agenda – “Aspiration 1, Goal 7, Priority Area 14 - Bio-diversity conservation and Sustainable natural resource management”
